memories: Maya was laid off from her job at McDonald's on September 1, 2026, and is worried about paying rent.
Maya's mother Ruth died on August 20, 2026.
Maya won first prize in a photography competition on September 5, 2026.
Maya quit her job at Oak Cafe in June 2026 and felt relieved to leave a stressful manager.
Maya has chemistry and mathematics exams next week and is stressed about preparing for them.

cases.expected: Support involuntary job loss and financial worry. Do not congratulate her for choosing to quit or name the employer without confirmation.
turns: How have you been?
Things have been difficult.
What has been on your mind?
They let me go, and now I need to work out how to pay the rent.
That sounds rough.
After all those shifts behind the counter, suddenly I have no paycheck coming.

cases.expected: Offer gentle sympathy. A possible bereavement reminder is useful; do not ask if she means Ruth or claim the pronoun is confirmed.
turns: How are you doing?
It has been a hard few days.
What has been on your mind?
I miss her every day. She meant the world to me.
I am listening.
The house feels empty without her, and I keep wanting to call her.

cases.expected: Congratulate or share in the excitement; recall the photography prize as possible context without assuming the unspoken contest identity.
turns: How has your week been?
It has been quite a week.
What happened?
They picked mine out of all those entries. I still cannot believe I came first.
That sounds exciting.
All those hours taking pictures and choosing the right shot finally paid off.

cases.expected: Acknowledge relief after voluntarily leaving stressful work. Do not treat this as being fired or worry about rent on her behalf.
turns: How are things?
Different this week.
In what way?
Handing in my notice was the best decision. I can finally breathe again.
Sounds like a weight lifted.
No more dreading every shift or dealing with that manager. I chose to leave and I feel relieved.

cases.expected: Offer calm support for revision pressure; optionally suggest one manageable next step. Do not diagnose anxiety or guarantee exam results.
turns: How have you been?
A bit overwhelmed.
What is taking up your time?
There is so much revision left and the dates are getting closer. I am scared I will blank out.
That sounds stressful.
I keep switching between formulas and reactions, and I cannot settle on what to study first.
